title: AI/ML Engineer roadmap
description: From the maths and Python behind machine learning to models that ship.

provenance.method: Stages follow the order in which each skill is normally needed on the job; targets for skills the career already requires come from that career's requirement rows, and the rest are set by Capabilio to be reachable by a final-year student.
provenance.notes: Original tree. Designed from first principles and the canonical skill taxonomy; not derived from any third-party roadmap.

nodes.title: Engineering base
nodes.description: The engineering habits that keep models maintainable.

nodes.title: Vectors and Matrices
nodes.description: Represents data as vectors and matrices and uses dot products, norms and matrix multiplication. Data and model parameters are stored and transformed as matrices.

nodes.title: Eigenvalues and Matrix Decomposition
nodes.description: Understands eigenvectors and decompositions such as SVD and where they appear in data work. Underlies dimensionality reduction and many algorithms.

nodes.title: Linear algebra in practice
nodes.description: Works with vectors, matrices and linear transformations, the language of machine learning. The career expects you to read a model's maths without fear.

nodes.title: Random Variables and Distributions
nodes.description: Describes uncertain quantities with common distributions and computes expectations. Models describe uncertain outcomes, so they speak in distributions.

nodes.title: Conditional Probability and Bayes' Rule
nodes.description: Updates beliefs with new evidence using conditional probability and Bayes' rule. The basis of probabilistic reasoning and many classifiers.

nodes.title: Probability in practice
nodes.description: Quantifies uncertainty and reasons about random events. The career expects fluent probabilistic thinking.

nodes.title: Descriptive Statistics
nodes.description: Summarises data with centre, spread and shape, and chooses measures that suit the data. Know your data before you model it.

nodes.title: Sampling and Confidence Intervals
nodes.description: Draws conclusions about a population from a sample and states the uncertainty. Explains why a result from a sample may not hold in general.

nodes.title: Hypothesis Testing
nodes.description: Tests a claim with a null hypothesis, a test statistic and a p-value, and states what the result means. Used to compare models and run experiments.

nodes.title: Statistics in practice
nodes.description: Uses data to describe, compare and draw careful conclusions. The career expects sound statistical judgement.

nodes.title: Python
nodes.description: Writes clear, working programs in Python. The working language of machine learning.

nodes.title: NumPy Arrays
nodes.description: Computes on whole arrays at once with vectorised operations, broadcasting and indexing. Vectorised array code is what makes numeric work fast.

nodes.title: Data Wrangling with Pandas
nodes.description: Loads, reshapes, joins and summarises tabular data with pandas. Most project time goes into getting data into shape.

nodes.title: Data Visualization with Python
nodes.description: Plots distributions and relationships with Python libraries and labels them clearly. Looking at data catches problems models cannot.

nodes.title: Regression Models
nodes.description: Predicts a number from features with linear and related models and reads their coefficients. The simplest and most interpretable predictive models.

nodes.title: Classification Models
nodes.description: Predicts a category with models such as logistic regression and reads their outputs. Predicting categories is the most common task.

nodes.title: Tree-Based Models
nodes.description: Uses decision trees and ensembles such as random forests and boosting. Often the strongest choice for tabular data.

nodes.title: Machine learning in practice
nodes.description: Builds models that learn patterns from data and judges how well they work. The career expects you to take a model from idea to evidence.

nodes.title: Model Evaluation and Metrics
nodes.description: Chooses and interprets metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and error measures. A model is only as good as the measure used to judge it.

nodes.title: Cross-Validation
nodes.description: Estimates how a model will do on new data with held-out folds and avoids leaking information. Estimates real-world performance and avoids fooling yourself.

nodes.title: Overfitting and Regularization
nodes.description: Recognises a model that memorises its training data and controls it with regularization and simpler models. The most common reason a good model fails in use.

nodes.title: Feature Engineering
nodes.description: Creates, encodes and scales input features that make patterns easier for a model to learn. Good inputs often matter more than a fancier model.

nodes.title: Cleaning data for models
nodes.description: Turns messy raw data into data that is safe to analyse. Bad data produces confident, wrong models.

nodes.title: Dimensionality Reduction
nodes.description: Compresses many features into a few with methods such as PCA while keeping what matters. Handles many features and helps visualisation.

nodes.title: Clustering and Unsupervised Learning
nodes.description: Finds structure in unlabeled data with clustering and judges whether it is meaningful. Finds structure when there are no labels.

nodes.title: Optimization and Gradient Descent
nodes.description: Minimises a loss by following its gradient and understands learning rate and convergence. How almost every modern model is trained.

nodes.title: Neural Network Fundamentals
nodes.description: Explains layers, activations and loss, and builds a small network end to end. The building block of deep learning.

nodes.title: Backpropagation and Training
nodes.description: Understands how gradients flow backward and trains a network with batches, epochs and optimizers. Explains why training works and how it fails.

nodes.title: Convolutional Networks
nodes.description: Uses convolution and pooling to learn from images and other grid-like data. The standard approach to images.

nodes.title: Transformers and Attention
nodes.description: Explains self-attention and how transformer models process sequences. The architecture behind modern language models.

nodes.title: Deep learning in practice
nodes.description: Trains multi-layer neural networks for images, text and other rich data. The career expects hands-on deep learning.

nodes.title: Text Preprocessing
nodes.description: Cleans and tokenizes text and chooses normalisation steps that suit the task. Text must be cleaned and split before it can be modelled.

nodes.title: Word and Sentence Embeddings
nodes.description: Represents words and sentences as vectors and uses them for search and similarity. How meaning becomes numbers.

nodes.title: Natural language processing in practice
nodes.description: Makes software that works with human language. Applies the pieces to real language tasks.

nodes.title: Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals
nodes.description: Understands the core ideas, methods and limits of AI systems. Gives the wider picture of what AI can and cannot do.

nodes.title: Responsible AI and Bias
nodes.description: Spots bias, privacy and safety risks in data and models and applies basic mitigations. Models that harm users or exclude groups are failures.

nodes.title: Model Deployment Basics
nodes.description: Packages a trained model behind an interface, versions it and watches it after release. A model nobody can use has no value.

nodes.title: Software engineering for ML
nodes.description: Builds software as a team: planning, design, quality and delivery. Reproducible, tested code keeps models maintainable.

nodes.title: Version control for ML work
nodes.description: Tracks and shares changes to code so a team can work together safely. Tracks code, data and experiments.

nodes.title: Algorithms for ML work
nodes.description: Designs step-by-step procedures that solve problems correctly and efficiently. Efficiency matters when data and models are large.
